description:
From the fz-kdt.119 cold review (2026-09-01). The review's
FZ_DEBUG_TUPLE_SHAPE probe -- a runtime counter firing when a value
passes an arm's test while lying outside the surface that arm's body
was compiled for -- found TEN fixtures in one corpus pass (00183 x16,
00230 x16, 00418 x4, 00419 x16, 00420 x81, hof_three_distinct x6,
predicate_search x7, take_drop_split x81, receive_map_pattern x1,
unused_range_binding x4). The static fz-kdt.129 gate sees 19 pairwise
escapes on 14 hand-picked fixtures; this sees the real thing, on the
production path, corpus-wide, cheaply. Land it as a permanent
env-gated tripwire (FZ_STRESS_ASSERT_SURFACE_MEMBERSHIP: count, or
hard-error under the flag) + a corpus sweep recipe. This is the
fourth demonstration that corpus stdout sweeps pass while dispatch
defects ship -- this instrument is the corrective. fz-kdt.119 lands
it in-story per its gate list; this ticket tracks the corpus-sweep
integration and the triage of the ten findings (each is a latent
blind-routing site; the two x81 are the take_drop blocker ticket).
title: A dynamic surface-membership tripwire: the instrument the dispatch class has been missing
